# LeSearch AI — feature-to-code map

This is the index of every **implemented, user-facing** feature in LeSearch AI, one
table per surface, with the file(s) that implement it and the self-check that proves
it still works. It is a map onto the code, not the spec — for what the product *is
meant to be* (names, non-goals, open decisions), read
[docs/product/PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) first; this file exists so a reviewer or a new
agent can find "where does X live" and "what proves X still works" without reading
every screen file.

**How it stays current.** It is generated by hand from the committed maps, which are
generated from the tree:

```sh
python3 scripts/codemap-index.py   # rebuilds docs/agents/CODEMAP.md, CHECKS.md, CONTRACTS.md, SYMBOLS.md
sh scripts/codemap.sh              # the above, plus `graphify update .`
```

Re-run `codemap-index.py` after adding a file, and re-check this document by hand
after adding or removing a screen, a CLI verb, a daemon route, or a check — the same
discipline `scripts/check-product-spec.sh` holds `PRODUCT.md` to.

A "Covered by" cell names a real `scripts/check-*` file from
[docs/agents/CHECKS.md](../agents/CHECKS.md). An em dash (`—`) means the feature has no
dedicated self-check today, not that it is untested by hand.

## iPhone app (Xcode target `MeshWatch`, iOS 26)

| Feature | What it does (one sentence, user's words) | Where it lives (file paths, comma-separated) | Covered by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Machines tab | See every paired machine on one list, with live stats and a live thumbnail of its screen; tap a thumbnail to take control | iOS/ContentView.swift, iOS/MeshStore.swift | — |
| No machines (first run) | The empty state before anything is paired, with one button into pairing | iOS/PairMachineView.swift | — |
| Machine detail | Open a machine's screen and control, files, load at a glance (memory/disk/CPU gauges, heaviest processes), sessions, setup and power, all from one screen | iOS/ContentView.swift, iOS/MachineStatsView.swift | — |
| Pair a machine | Turn a code or a QR the Mac/Linux box printed into a paired machine | iOS/PairMachineView.swift, iOS/PairingScanner.swift | check-pairing.swift |
| Monitor (usage + events) | See usage/limits per AI provider and a feed of agent events, newest first, from the bell in every tab | iOS/ContentView.swift, Shared/LimitHelpers.swift | check-limit-helpers.swift, check-usage-alert-identity.sh |
| Sessions / new session | List an agent's sessions on a machine and start a new one with a chosen CLI, working directory and task | iOS/TerminalView.swift | check-harness-picker.sh |
| Session limit hand-off | When an agent's usage limit blocks it mid-task, offer to continue the same conversation with a different installed agent | iOS/TerminalView.swift, Shared/LimitHelpers.swift | check-limit-helpers.swift |
| Session peek | Read a session's recent output, and answer it if it is waiting on you | iOS/TerminalView.swift | — |
| Agent chat | Have a conversation with a running coding agent — bubbles, decision cards, tool-result cards, artifacts, thinking disclosure, and a menu of an agent's own on-screen prompt read as tappable buttons | iOS/AgentChatView.swift, Shared/RiskClassifier.swift, Shared/Models.swift | — |
| Terminal tab | A live terminal into a session, streamed over the daemon's own bridge, with a read-only fallback peek when the bridge is down | iOS/TerminalView.swift | check-harness-picker.sh, check-phone-input-and-wake.sh, check-watch-terminal-wiring.sh |
| Screen & control (Remote) | See the machine's screen live, drag/tap/zoom it with real trackpad gestures, and type with the machine's own keyboard modifiers, launcher and terminal one tap away | iOS/RemoteScreenView.swift | check-inspect-crop.sh, check-mesh-chords.sh, check-remote-screen-gestures.sh |
| Files | Browse a machine's filesystem and read a file on the phone — Markdown rendered, HTML shown, code and text sized by pinch | iOS/FileBrowserView.swift, iOS/FileViewer.swift | — |
| Apps tab | Every app an agent built for you, across every paired machine, in one list — open it or install it | iOS/AppsLibraryView.swift | check-apps-ota.sh |
| Mesh Apps (per machine) | See and install the apps an agent published or registered on one specific machine, from inside a session | iOS/TerminalView.swift | check-apps-serve.sh, check-apps-ota.sh |
| Report a problem → LeSearch AI | Write what happened in your own words and send a redacted diagnostic bundle (app build, machines, daemon versions, recent events, the last error), with an optional photo/video attachment, or save it to a machine for an agent to read | iOS/FeedbackView.swift, iOS/LeSearchCloud.swift | check-feedback-cloud.sh, check-feedback-redact.swift, check-feedback-pipeline.sh |
| Account (optional sign in) | Create or sign in to an optional LeSearch AI account so a problem report can be tied back to you later | iOS/AccountView.swift, iOS/LeSearchCloud.swift | check-feedback-cloud.sh |
| Guides | The steps no app can do for you — pairing, developer mode, permissions, a Linux desktop, running an agent overnight | iOS/GuidesView.swift | — |
| Exposed secrets | See what the daemon redacted before it left your machine, by kind and fingerprint, and mark it rotated | iOS/ExposedSecretsScreen.swift | check-redact.sh |
| Voice input | Dictate into the composer with a live editable transcript; recordings kept so you can transcribe again | iOS/VoiceInput.swift, iOS/VoiceTranscriber.swift, Shared/VoiceSegments.swift | check-voice-accumulate.sh |

| App lock | Lock the app behind Face ID / Touch ID | iOS/AppLock.swift | — |

on-device transcription.

## `meshd` daemon routes (`install/payload/meshd/`, one per machine, port 8899)

Bearer-token auth on every route except `GET /health`, `ANY /a/*` and the pairing
routes (which use the pair code or loopback as their own credential); see
[docs/agents/CONTRACTS.md](../agents/CONTRACTS.md) for the full route table with line
numbers.

| Feature | What it does (one sentence, user's words) | Where it lives (file paths, comma-separated) | Covered by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routing, capabilities, Origin/Host guard | The route table itself, the `GET /health` capability list clients gate on, and the DNS-rebinding defence that runs before auth | install/payload/meshd/server.ts | check-mesh-auth.sh, check-host-guard.sh, check-daemon-050.sh |
| Auth | Fail-closed bearer-token check with a loopback exemption a machine owner can disable | install/payload/meshd/auth.ts, install/payload/meshd/loopback-trust.ts | check-mesh-auth.sh, check-pair-auth.sh |
| Doctor | `GET /doctor` / `POST /doctor/fix` — one report that tests whether the machine is actually usable, not just whether it claims to be | install/payload/meshd/doctor.ts | check-mesh-doctor.sh |
| Input / remote control | Pointer, keyboard, media keys, window list, power, clipboard, screen capture and regions, on macOS and Linux | install/payload/meshd/input.ts, install/payload/meshd/input-linux.ts | check-mesh-input.sh, check-mesh-chords.sh, check-linux-desktop.sh, check-daemon-050.sh |
| Push notifications | Direct APNs push from the daemon (no cloud relay), with one-buzz dedupe and Live Activity push-to-start | install/payload/meshd/push.ts | check-mesh-push.sh, check-alert-gating.swift |
| Pairing | One-use 8-character codes (10-minute expiry) that turn into a real device token, plus the QR encoder | install/payload/meshd/pair.ts, install/payload/meshd/qr.ts | check-mesh-pair.sh, check-pair-qr.sh, check-pairing.swift |
| Files | Browse a machine's filesystem and read/write files over HTTP, plus the daemon-served file page | install/payload/meshd/files.ts, install/payload/meshd/files.html | — |
| Knowledge base | Durable, searchable shared memory for agents (SQLite FTS5), with read federation across paired hosts | install/payload/meshd/kb.ts | check-kb-federation.sh |
| Mesh Apps (hosting) | Serve a published web app token-free, register a native build, and hand out wireless (OTA) install links | install/payload/meshd/apps.ts | check-apps-serve.sh, check-apps-ota.sh |
| Transcript chat | Read a running coding agent's own transcript as a structured conversation for the phone's Agent Chat screen | install/payload/meshd/chat.ts | — |
| Hand-off | Move a session to a different agent CLI via `HANDOFF.md` in the working directory | install/payload/meshd/handoff.ts | check-handoff.sh |
| Local brain | Report which local model server answers on this machine and what it can do, without starting or stopping one | install/payload/meshd/brain.ts | check-brain.sh |
| Redaction | Strip secrets out of every line before it leaves the machine (push, events, chat), and count exposures by fingerprint, never by value | install/payload/meshd/redact.ts | check-redact.sh |
| Codex state | Read why a Codex session stopped and when its usage window resets | install/payload/meshd/codex-state.ts | check-codex-state.sh |
| Multiplexer adapters | Run and control agent sessions over rmux/tmux/cmux/herdr | install/payload/meshd/cmux-bridge.ts, install/payload/meshd/herdr.ts | check-herdr-sessions.sh |
| Wake-on-LAN | Power a sleeping machine back on from the wrist | install/payload/meshd/wol.ts | check-wol.sh |
| Telemetry | One anonymized heartbeat a day at most, and nothing else | install/payload/meshd/telemetry.ts | — |
| Terminal bridge (`:7820`) | The token-gated WebSocket the phone's xterm.js terminal actually attaches to | install/payload/rmux-bridge/src/server.ts | check-bridge-auth.sh, check-package-mesh-install.sh |
| Wake / phone push registration | Register this device for push, and let another surface wake it | install/payload/meshd/push.ts, install/payload/meshd/server.ts | check-mesh-push.sh |

## Hosted "Apps" (Mesh Apps)

Apps an agent builds *for the user* — a static web app or a native build — served and
installed off the paired machine, no app-store round trip.

| Feature | What it does (one sentence, user's words) | Where it lives (file paths, comma-separated) | Covered by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Publish a web app | `mesh apps publish <dir> --slug --name` serves a static web app token-free at `/a/<slug>-<key>/` | install/payload/meshd/apps.ts, install/payload/bin/mesh | check-apps-serve.sh |
| Register a native build | `mesh apps add --app` registers a built native app (iPhone/iPad/Watch/Mac/Vision, read off the bundle) so it shows up on every paired device | install/payload/meshd/apps.ts, install/payload/bin/mesh | check-mesh-apps.sh |
| Wireless (OTA) install | Package a device build into a valid signed `.ipa` and hand out an `itms-services` install link — no cable | install/payload/meshd/apps.ts, install/payload/bin/mesh | check-apps-ota.sh |
| Cross-machine apps library | Every app built anywhere on the fleet, one list, newest first, grouped by name | iOS/AppsLibraryView.swift | check-apps-ota.sh |
| Install from a running session | Open or install an app an agent just built, from inside its chat / terminal screen | iOS/TerminalView.swift | check-apps-serve.sh |

## Not built yet (do not document as features)

These are named in `PRODUCT.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `docs/` but have no shipping
implementation today — do not treat a mention of them elsewhere as evidence they exist.

- **Needle 2 on-device intent** (`PRODUCT.md` §9) — proposed. The tool catalogue and
  acceptance suite exist (`intent/mesh-tools.json`, `intent/cases.jsonl`,
  `scripts/check-intent.sh`) as a **measurement**, not a shipped feature: the check
  skips itself when no `needle` binary is present, and no app code calls it. No wrist
  phrase is turned into a daemon call today.
- **`mesh-code`** (`PRODUCT.md` §2, PR #119) — a proposed local coding agent driven
  through the daemon. No `mesh-code` binary exists in `install/payload/bin/`.
- **Permissions window v2** (`PRODUCT.md` §8) — the target design (`required`,
  `usedBy`, `checkable`, `requestable` fields on every `/doctor` check, grouped rows,
  per-row *Request*) is specified but not implemented; `install/payload/meshd/doctor.ts`
  does not emit those fields today, and `MeshDesktop/PermissionsView.swift` is still the
  flat list the spec calls "today."
- **Mac menu bar app distribution** — the app itself is built and functional
  (`MeshDesktop/`), but it ships as a local `.app` only; there is no notarized release
  in the `mesh-install` payload or App Store listing yet (`PRODUCT.md` §3: "built, not
  distributed").
- **A cloud relay** — explicit non-goal (`PRODUCT.md` §10). The phone always talks
  directly to a machine's own daemon.
- **VNC** — explicit non-goal; screen/input already goes over the daemon's own
  bearer-authed HTTP.
- **A general account system** — `PRODUCT.md` §10 lists this as a non-goal for machine
  access (pairing is a printed code, not an account). The new "Account (optional sign
  in)" feature above is scoped narrowly to the feedback pipeline (tying a problem
  report back to a person) and does not gate pairing or machine access; worth watching
  that it does not grow into the thing §10 rules out.

## Not verified

- The exact wiring from Settings → "Report a problem" / "Account" was confirmed by
  grep (`iOS/ContentView.swift:1335`, `:1352`), not by running the app, since this
  worktree has no simulator session in progress.
- `docs/agents/CONTRACTS.md`'s capability table shows several capabilities (`events`,
  `newPane`, `usage`, `agents`, `cmux`, `herdr`, `tailscale`, `kb`, `files`, `push`,
  `pair`, `doctor`) as "nothing gates it" client-side — they are always assumed present
  rather than feature-flagged. Their routes are still real and listed above; this note
  is only that the client never checks for their absence.
